messages.author: 73a4bd09ccef7d80
messages.subject: Is this a correct model for my data?  [Time sensitive]
parts:
Hi there,


Study summary:  In my study, I asked the participants to rate how much they  attended to a vibration pattern on their body.  They used a slider to answer the question. The slider range was between [0,100] with zero indicating easily and 100 indicating very hard. The study was done with 36 participants, each rating their experience 18 times. The raw values of "Attend" is shown in figure 1. 

Given that my dependent variable is inflated with zeros, I decided to use the following model to fit my data with.  Though, I am not sure if I set the parameters in bold correctly. Would you please confirm whether I did it right please?

NA_fit1 <- glmmTMB(Attend ~ Bodysite + Pattern * Strength + (1 |id), data=data1, dispformula =~0, ziformula=~1, family=poisson)


Thank you again!
P

This probably belongs on r-sig-mix...@r-project.org: as the
glmmTMB readme suggests,

- r-sig-mix...@r-project.org for general questions about glmmTMB
usage and mixed models
- https://github.com/glmmTMB/glmmTMB/issues for bug, infelicity, and
wishlist reporting
- https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/tmb-users for TMB-specific questions
- maintainer e-mail only for urgent/private communications

It looks like your model is OK, but I'd suggest modeling Attend/100
as Beta-distributed, rather than modeling Attend as 100 - it doesn't
really seem like a very Poisson-ish process. Also, you should
probably consider some additional random effects (like BodySite|id, or
1|id/BodySite ...)

Hi Ben,

Thank you for the quick response.

I ran into two issues here: 

1. For Attend to fit under a beta distribution, the following has to be fulfilled:  0 <Attend /100< 1. Though currently  0 <= Attend/100 <=1.  
2. Even if Attend/100 first between zero and 1,  I get the following error when I construct the model: 

Attend_fit1 <- glmmTMB(Attend/100 ~ Bodysite + Pattern * Strength + (1 |id) + (Bodysite|id), data=data1, dispformula =~0, ziformula=~1, family=beta_family())

Error in mkTMBStruc(formula, ziformula, dispformula, combForm, mf, fr, : ~0 dispersion not implemented for ‘beta’ family

I also found this bit of a tex on how to deal with continuous inflated with zero data (please see the attachment). 

I am not an expert on this topic. Could you help me make progress, please? 

Thank you again!
P

Hi Ben,

I think I figured it out? 

Attend_fit1 <- glmmTMB((Attend/100* 35 + .5) /36 ~ Bodysite + Pattern * Strength + (1 |id), data=data1,  ziformula=~1, family=beta_family(link = "logit"))


N (sample size ) = 36 participants. 

Please let me know if this is correct. 

The formula to move the [0,1] to (0,1) mapping was based on this paper: https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/8517/79099a662b91c8153a9a40e069f0276eecbc.pdf

I have one more question. Do you think with the data that looks like the attached image, I can construct the same model as the attend (with beta distribution assumption)?  


Diff_PA_NA_fit2 <- glmmTMB(((Diff_PA_NA+100)/200* 35 + .5) /36 ~ Bodysite + Pattern * Strength + (1 |id), data=data1,  ziformula=~1, family=beta_family(link = "logit"))


PA stands for values of positive affect. The range of the value is [0,100].
NA stands for values of negative affect. The range of the value is [0,100]. The NA is inflated with zeros. 
The idea is that PA - NA should reflect the valence of an emotion that the participants experienced when receiving the haptic vibration on their body. 


Thanks again for the help!!

don't post sensitive information)

images, data or very complex code, consider uploading it somewhere and
posting a public link

general audience
